admissibility_policy.meaning: admissible means explicit, scoped, and testable or constitutive; it does not mean empirically true
admissibility_policy.empirical_closure_rule: a real-world application requires at least one empirical_study reference and at least one manifest-backed machine check

assumptions.statement: Visited vertices cannot be revisited and the forward feasible set is history dependent.
assumptions.scope: All IDP traversal claims using condition C1.
assumptions.role: Defines endogenous feasibility rather than asserting an empirical frequency.

testability.criterion: An application is outside scope when reversals, recalls, or costless backtracking are feasible.

assumptions.statement: The focal local theorem uses a degree-two start with a terminal trap neighbor.
assumptions.scope: Canonical and five-state local examples, not arbitrary graphs.
assumptions.role: Makes the routing mechanism finite and exactly enumerable.

testability.criterion: The assumption fails when the trap branch has further feasible continuation or the start has additional available neighbors.

assumptions.statement: Reward signals are Gaussian and reveal rewards but not the realized percolation topology.
assumptions.role: Separates reward information from structural knowledge.

testability.criterion: Recompute the claim under non-Gaussian noise and under signals that include edge-state information.

assumptions.statement: The greedy agent ranks currently available neighbors by posterior immediate reward rather than continuation value.
assumptions.role: Defines the misspecified objective that can create the reversal.

testability.criterion: Choice data can compare immediate-reward rankings with continuation-value rankings at otherwise matched decision nodes.

assumptions.statement: Vertex rewards are independent Uniform[0,1] draws where closed-form order statistics are used.
assumptions.scope: Cluster-size welfare formulas and local trap prevalence calculations.
assumptions.role: Provides exact order-statistic and ranking-reversal probabilities.

testability.criterion: Replace the reward law and recompute order statistics; no empirical universality is asserted.

assumptions.statement: Edges are blocked independently with common probability p.
assumptions.scope: Lattice, Erdos-Renyi thinning, and configuration-model percolation claims.
assumptions.role: Matches the independent bond-percolation theorems used as external premises.

testability.criterion: Correlated or targeted failures require a separate model and are outside the cited threshold formulas.

assumptions.statement: A scalar kappa interpolates between immediate-reward and continuation-value objectives.
assumptions.role: Defines a one-dimensional reduced-form cognition family.

testability.criterion: Estimate kappa from repeated routing choices and report sensitivity to alternative interpolation rules.

assumptions.statement: On the five-state benchmark, a structurally aware agent observes the bridge state with probability 1 - 2^(-kappa) and otherwise observes an erasure; revealed and erased signals use the explicit routing rule in Proposition prop:threshold-five-state.
assumptions.scope: Only the finite five-state cognition and reward-precision propositions; it does not identify the Gaussian topology signal or the depth-d trap-tree model.
assumptions.role: Provides a fully specified Blackwell-ordered finite experiment whose routing and welfare are exactly machine checkable.

testability.criterion: Recompute the finite theorem under alternative reveal functions or non-erasure signal alphabets; do not transfer the endpoint formulas without re-proving them.

assumptions.statement: A scalar alpha weights instrumental reward relative to an independent sentimental component.
assumptions.role: Defines the paper's non-instrumental preference perturbation.

testability.criterion: Calibrate alpha from choices with independently varied monetary and sentimental attributes and test alternative dependence structures.

assumptions.statement: Population welfare aggregates individual welfare over a specified distribution of cognitive parameters.

testability.criterion: The parameter distribution must be estimated or supplied, and conclusions must be sensitivity-tested over alternative distributions.

assumptions.statement: The Bayesian benchmark observes the realized percolation state before optimizing a traversal strategy.

testability.criterion: The benchmark does not apply when the agent observes only a prior over topology.

assumptions.statement: The Bayesian-naive five-state agent routes using a prior-only continuation estimate with perceived blocking probability hat-p.
assumptions.role: Defines a distinct misspecification from topology omission.

testability.criterion: Routing choices must remain signal independent at the start node and identify the implied prior threshold.

assumptions.statement: The network sequence is an uncorrelated configuration model with a power-law degree law and the regularity conditions required by the cited threshold theorem.
assumptions.scope: Power-law application only; targeted removal and arbitrary empirical networks are excluded.
assumptions.role: States the model class on which moment-based percolation criteria are valid.

testability.criterion: Check degree-law fit, degree correlations, finite-size cutoff, and removal mechanism before applying the threshold formula.
